6.description: Saskatoon's successful loading zone pilot received an update, which the Accessibility Advisory Committee will now review for information.

21.description: Saskatoon adopted new policies for accessible loading zones, establishing a request process, eligibility criteria, and design standards for schools, health facilities, and community services. Residential locations are excluded.

chips.text: Received as information
Committee members expressed disappointment over the limited number of new accessible parking spaces.
People using mobility devices will have improved access to schools and care homes.
Snow removal plans for new accessible parking zones remain undecided.
Pilot project participants expressed high satisfaction with the new accessible loading zones.
Existing accessible loading zone provisions will remain until more spaces are built.

17.description: Council is reviewing the adequacy of dedicated loading zones for people with mobility issues, considering if the current 2% allocation in pay parking zones is sufficient, especially on Broadway.

chips.text: Councillor questioned the 2% accessible parking target, suggesting 4-5% is more realistic.
Whether the 2% accessible parking target is sufficient for Broadway remains an open question.
A delegate shared personal struggles with loading zones, advocating for more accessible spaces.
Staff committed to revisiting the 2% accessible parking target if user needs are not met.

19.description: Saskatoon will increase on-street accessible parking, but the proposed 2% cap was deemed insufficient, especially for areas like Broadway. The city will gather more feedback and revisit the cap.

chips.text: Approved
Councillor questioned the 2% cap, suggesting 4-5% is more realistic.
People with mobility challenges and out-of-town visitors are affected.
How to accurately measure demand, especially from out-of-town users, remains unclear.
Public expressed support for loading zones, but concern over prolonged use.
Map accessibility for visually impaired people was raised as a concern.
Staff won't change loading zone use until sufficient dedicated space.

7.description: Council approved categories for the 2026 Work Plan, focusing on Deafblind Services, transit, accessibility, and safety in downtown and Bus Rapid Transit areas.

chips.text: Approved
Work plan categories address accessibility for Deafblind individuals and Access Transit users.

20.description: The committee will disband standing subcommittees due to limited activity, opting instead to address issues as a committee of the whole or by forming ad hoc subcommittees for specific matters.

chips.text: Approved
Members discussed current capacity and interest in continuing standing subcommittees for 2026.

9.description: Council received a statement detailing current expenditures for the committee's information. This item provides an overview of city spending.

chips.text: Received as information
